Plan for Phase 68a at 3a54c92: docs/phases/headless-watcher-hands-an-approved-plan-to-the-lead.md. It opens with the findings of a real cycle run through the cockpit in headless mode on 2026-09-20 (scratch project; watch-log excerpt and a findings table saying which phase takes each one).

Two engine fixes, no UI:
1. In headless mode _handle_done has no branch: after a plan approval it logs 'Sending completion notice to claude...' and sends nothing, so a single-phase headless run stops until a human clicks Start (in iTerm2 the typed notice keeps it moving). Proposed: headless + single-phase + plan approved → apply the same state transition full-roadmap already applies there (turn lead, status ready, command '<handoff> start <phase> impl', expected_seq + the two staleness guards), through one helper shared with _try_roadmap_advance. The engine already identifies and verifies start commands (TurnIdentity.is_start), so headless.py is untouched. Impl approval in single-phase is unchanged (the run stops; that default is Phase 70's to change). No advance on a watcher restart over an already-done state. Tab/tmux/notify modes unchanged. No config switch: it matches what tab watchers already do, and tagteam pause holds it.
2. A Phase 67 defect of mine, in 3.14.5: the beat is written only before tick(), so after a long turn 'watch status' reads STALE ('37s ago … nothing in flight', observed) until the next loop iteration. Fix: also beat when tick() returns, in both loops; the 5 s throttle makes that free for short ticks.

Please look hardest at: whether reusing the state transition (rather than spawning the lead straight from _handle_done) is right; the restart rule; and whether 'no switch' is acceptable given a project could have relied on the headless loop pausing after plan approval.

Verified while planning: roadmap check ok (76 phases, 32 edges; 68 now depends on 68a); gate check --skip-tests plan-doc ok. Nothing implemented.

Approved plan at 3a54c92. Reusing the guarded plan-to-implementation state transition is the right approach: it creates an ordinary owed lead turn visible to the engine, cockpit and pause handling, rather than introducing a second spawning path. The existing snapshot_identity/start verification supports the proposed command and impl-cycle target. Keeping the first-poll non-ready bootstrap rule avoids restarting work from historical approvals. No new switch is needed for this scoped completion of a phase already being run; document the changed behavior and pause option in the release note as proposed. Single-phase impl approval remains terminal.

Implementation details to preserve:
- Explicitly require state.get('run_mode', 'single-phase') == 'single-phase' for the new headless path. A None return from _try_roadmap_advance does not imply single-phase: full-roadmap also returns None after a stale-state guard or when roadmap metadata is absent. Do not retry the shared transition as a fallback in those cases; cover this boundary in the processor tests.
- The post-tick beat should represent the state after the tick when practical (a long headless turn may have changed phase/type/turn/seq). Retain the throttle and cover a long tick that changes state as well as the timestamp refresh. No new engine control flow is needed.
- Retain the explicit no-action first-tick test and seed a previously observed state in the normal advance test so these criteria are not contradictory.

Reviewed the current _try_roadmap_advance, _handle_done, bootstrap, and headless start-command verification. No implementation exists yet; no tests were run for this documentation-only review. No outstanding plan blockers or interjections.
